stem: Which scenario is a particularly poor-risk childhood cancer situation?

options.text: Stage IV neuroblastoma in a child older than 1 year
All acute lymphoblastic leukaemia regardless of cytogenetics
Localised rhabdomyosarcoma confined to one site

explanation: Stage IV neuroblastoma in a child older than 1 year is one of the particularly poor-risk childhood cancer situations. The other options are not listed as part of that highest-risk group in the stem’s clinical framing.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 123

rationale: Stage IV neuroblastoma over age 1 year is specifically identified as a very poor-risk childhood cancer situation, whereas the other options describe cancers or risk groups that are not included in that category.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because stage IV neuroblastoma in a child older than 1 year is explicitly recognised as a particularly poor-risk childhood cancer situation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because non-metastatic Ewing sarcoma is not in the highest-risk category described here.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because non-metastatic osteosarcoma is not one of the particularly poor-risk situations named here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the poor-risk group is not all ALL; it refers to ALL with adverse cytogenetics or other high-risk features.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because localised rhabdomyosarcoma confined to one site is not one of the particularly poor-risk situations listed here.
